dedupe_keys.name: maps multimodal analysis port simulation discrete event

description: Multimodal Analysis Port Simulation (MAPS) is a modular discrete-event simulation framework for port operations across container, liquid bulk and dry bulk terminals. It models a port with an anchorage area, a navigation channel, terminals and landside connections by truck, rail and pipeline, with container, tanker and dry bulk vessels, and each terminal is a SimPy process with its own resources and queues. It is designed for planning, bottleneck detection and what-if scenarios using real-world inputs and calibration, with scripts for main runs, bottleneck analysis and breakpoint analysis, a simulation manual and input data for a hypothetical generic port. It was developed by the Simulation, Pricing, Autonomous Vehicles, Routing and Traffic Assignment (SPARTA) Lab at The University of Texas at Austin, with Debojjal Bagchi and Kyle Bathgate named in the licence. Coverage is generic: users adjust the layout and inputs for their own port. Access: free on GitHub under the MIT licence as a public v0.1 beta. Caveats: it is a beta still under testing and development, and the bundled example is a hypothetical port. It supports port capacity planning, bottleneck and disruption analysis and landside interface studies, and complements the UK port congestion scores catalogued here.
